play.description: Kevin Durant's mid-range game remains basketball's most reliable weapon, especially when the Rockets need a bucket. With Houston trailing 111-108 and just 9 seconds left in overtime at Toyota Center, KD takes matters into his own hands. The future Hall of Famer rises up from 12 feet with his signature pullup jumper, the ball finding nothing but net to cut the deficit to one. Durant's 35-point masterpiece on 54% shooting powered Houston to a 117-113 victory on November 16, 2025.

At the heart of the Brooklyn Nets’ unforgettable push to contend for a title is nine-time All-Star and franchise catalyst Kevin Durant. Durant runs the floor as his teammates work in masterful lockstep to recover a steal against the Cleveland Cavaliers then rises up to throw down an off-glass alley-oop from teammate Mike James. Durant finished the May 16, 2021 contest with 23 points, eight rebounds and 13 assists.

21-point deficits and never-before-seen box scores on the Denver Nuggets’ side might’ve had the Phoenix Suns on the ropes, but if the last 17 seasons have proven anything, it’s that a fighting chance always remains under Kevin Durant’s supervision. Undaunted by the sight of multiple bigs awaiting his pick-and-roll decision, Durant leaves Aaron Gordon in the dust, rejecting a screen with a shifty crossover that eliminates two sizable defenders. Finding the game’s “difficulty” slightly lowered with only 6-foot-4 Jamal Murray left to overcome, Durant showcases get-a-bucket expertise, euro-stepping across the metaphorical globe for an around-the-rim reverse jam. Even Denver’s adversarial crowd couldn’t help audibly supporting Phoenix's four-time scoring champion on March 7, 2025, as he created the plays needed — including a game-tying 3-pointer at regulation’s end — to force a 21-point comeback. Only 10 days removed from playing in 2024-25’s highest-scoring regular-season game, Durant, even in a loss, relished the opportunity for something similar with a 29-point performance (on 10-of-19 shooting), alongside nine rebounds, five assists, and three 3-pointers.

Kevin Durant's midrange game remains basketball artistry at its finest. On Christmas Day, the future Hall of Famer turned the paint into his personal canvas against overmatched defenders. KD pulled up from his favorite spot and buried another textbook jumper, part of an efficient 8-for-14 shooting performance that included 4 three-pointers. Durant finished with 25 points, 8 assists, and a game-high plus-26 rating in the Rockets' 119-96 victory on December 25, 2025.

You think sending a double team to meet Kevin Durant in the corner is going to stop him from putting points on the board? Think again. After taking his defender off the dribble, the Brooklyn Nets superstar sets up on the baseline and buries an untouchable fadeaway. Durant dropped 38 points on 17-of-24 shooting in the October 24, 2021 affair.

Kevin Durant’s start was so hot that it all but finished the LA Clippers’ season before the halftime buzzer. The Golden State Warriors failed to eliminate the Clips despite Durant's 45 points two nights earlier in Game 5, so the star sniper decided to one-up himself with a legendary Game 6 closeout performance in the first-round playoff series. Durant kicked things off with an authoritative one-handed transition dunk, and his scorching first half also included four 3-pointers among his 12 made field goals. Whether he was converting triples from atop the key, difficult and-1 turnaround jumpers or runners in the lane, Durant’s vintage heat check game represented his most explosive postseason performance in an iconic career full of them. Once the dust settled, Durant had posted a playoff career-high 50 points on 15 of 26 from the field, 6 of 14 from downtown and 14 of 15 from the free throw line. He shot 12 of 17 before halftime alone as Golden State built an insurmountable 19-point lead, with his 38-point first-half eruption matching the second-most points ever scored in one half in postseason history. Durant added six rebounds and five assists in the 129-110 victory on April 26, 2019 as the Warriors won the series 4-2, with the two-time champion averaging 35 points across the six games.

Houston Rockets superstar Kevin Durant made history in his 18th NBA season, surpassing Michael Jordan for 5th place on the NBA's all-time scoring list. With the Rockets extending their lead in the fourth quarter at Toyota Center, Durant catches a pass from Reed Sheppard and knocks down a three-pointer that pushed his career point total to 32,294, officially passing His Airness. The milestone bucket helped Houston hold off Miami 123-122 in a thriller.

15 years later, there remains no defender nor scheme capable of consistently keeping Kevin Durant from getting to any bucket he desires. Never one to shy away from a high-profile duel against an elite at his position, the Phoenix Suns superstar finds himself in an unusual position midway through the fourth quarter: wide-open at the top of the key, with a free path to the rim. Taking a quick dish from a teammate, the 14-time All-Star makes his move, soaring through a sea of bodies before extending for a vicious one-handed tomahawk over the outstretched arms of a superstar counterpart to send the arena into a frenzy. Integrating his game perfectly to fit in big-time performances from his two All-Star teammates, Durant was business as usual, recording 28 points, 10 rebounds, one steal, two blocks, and one 3-pointer, fueling a primetime win over the Milwaukee Bucks on February 6, 2024.

Kevin Durant did not disappoint the fans who had waited nearly two months to witness his Phoenix Suns home debut. Healthy again after multiple injuries, the 13-time All-Star’s first home points stemmed from a Chris Paul feed into the post, with Durant then going to work backing down Jaden McDaniels before burying one of his patented turnaround jumpers. Durant posted 16 points, eight rebounds and four assists while helping the Suns pick up a 107-100 victory over the Minnesota Timberwolves on March 29, 2023.

Eighteen seasons in, Kevin Durant is still rewriting the record books. With 7:57 left in Q3 at Moda Center on January 9, 2026, Reed Sheppard finds the Slim Reaper spotting up beyond the arc. Durant catches in rhythm, elevates over his defender and buries a 25-foot three-pointer, pushing his career total to 31,422 points and past Wilt Chamberlain into seventh on the all-time scoring list. Portland's crowd rose to acknowledge greatness in a road uniform. Durant finished with 30 points, 12 rebounds and four assists.

While Kevin Durant's elite shooting touch defines his game, the future Hall of Famer reminds everyone he can attack the rim with equal ability. In his first game wearing Rockets red and playing against his former OKC squad, Durant faces a Thunder team protecting their home court on ring night. Down 1 with 1:15 left in the second overtime period, KD catches the ball on the move, accelerates past his defender and finishes a tough layup through contact.

If there were ever a drawback to scoring 30,000 points and securing more points than all but seven players in NBA history, it might arrive in the fact that one’s defensive highlight reel can sometimes be overlooked. In Year 17, and yet firmly in the mix alongside the league’s best rim protectors, Kevin Durant offers an example in defensive transition, swiveling his frame before forcefully sending Jaylen Clark’s layup attempt back to Minneapolis. Among 229 players to contest at least 150 paint shots in 2024-25, the Phoenix Suns’ superstar slots at No. 36, holding could-be slashers to 7.1 percentage points below their average. Phoenix would ultimately fall to the Minnesota Timberwolves in a rematch of last spring’s postseason, but the soon-to-be-named 15-time All-Star was nonetheless virtuosic. Unbothered by what the injury report called a “left thumb injury,” Durant’s hand proved steady on January 29, 2025, encouraging 33 points (on an incredibly-efficient 13-of-19 shooting), paired with seven assists, two steals, four swats, and four trifectas.

For even the most gifted first-year players, the process of getting acclimated to the NBA’s pressures can sometimes require some time. With a quick, unblockable release point perfectly matching that of his career’s trajectory, Kevin Durant used November 16, 2007 as confirmation to the Seattle SuperSonics that he was, in fact, not one of those players. Merely 10 games into his storybook career, Durant finds himself in prove-it position, with just 2.1 seconds remaining in a back-and-forth double overtime affair. Drifting towards the 3-point arc to provide his teammate with an outlet, the 2007 No. 2 pick leans back, as if in a recliner chair, before elevating into a breathtaking, off-balanced game-winner over Al Horford’s outstretched arms, stunning the Atlanta Hawks’ crowd in the process. The long-range bucket, appropriately, helped Seattle extend its streak to eight consecutive wins over Atlanta. Versatile in helping the SuperSonics overcome a game that featured 15 lead changes and 20 ties, Durant starred, putting in 21 points, three rebounds, two assists, three steals, three blocks, and one big-time 3-pointer.

Kevin Durant reminds everyone why he's one of the most versatile scorers in NBA history with his ability to attack the rim. With the Rockets clinging to a one-point lead late in the fourth quarter against their opponent, the future Hall of Famer receives a crisp pass from JD Davison and attacks the lane with purpose. Durant elevates and throws down a driving dunkt, extending Houston's lead to 105-104 with 3:24 remaining. The 7-footer finished with 28 points, 10 rebounds and 4 assists in the 119-113 victory on January 13, 2026.

Iconic hoop for an iconic hooper. With the fate of his squad’s season hanging in the balance, Brooklyn Nets star Kevin Durant flags down a cross-court inbound pass, drives on vaunted Milwaukee Bucks defender P.J. Tucker, then spins into an unforgettable fadeaway jumper. Durant’s deep two forced overtime in Game 7 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals and he finished the June 19, 2021 contest with 48 points.

It’s not easy crossing conferences and joining a new title contender in the middle of the season, but Kevin Durant has made a legendary career out of making the impossible look possible. In just eight contests following his trade to the Phoenix Suns, the 13-time All-Star has flashed the talent that puts this franchise’s upside through the roof.

Extraordinary enough in his craft to make one reconsider what qualifies as a “tough shot,” Kevin Durant used January 18, 2025 to break all of the rules, and the Detroit Pistons’ hearts, all at once. Unable to shake free of Detroit's new-and-improved form, neither on the scoreboard nor on-court, Durant keeps calm after Tobias Harris perfectly matches the screech on his brake-pumping behind-the-back dribble. Equivalent to that of a “select your difficulty” video game character programmed with counters for every move, Durant merely pivots inside, working a stealthy reverse spin that frees his vision for a cold-blooded 12-footer. Humorously pressing mute on the “DEFENSE” chants of Detroit’s home crowd, Durant’s midrange bucket, poetically, had deep implications on the game’s result, as the Phoenix Suns survived a four-point shootout. Producer of big-time buckets throughout, the four-time scoring champion treated box scores to 36 points (on 13-of-27 shooting), seven rebounds, five assists, two steals, three steals, and two triples.

After waiting five long years to get back to the NBA Finals, Kevin Durant wasn’t about to hesitate when the stakes were at their highest. Back in the championship round in 2017 – his first season with the Golden State Warriors –  Durant left little room for a second consecutive Cleveland Cavaliers Finals comeback, boldly drilling a monumental bucket to take a stranglehold on Game 3 and the series. After corralling a defensive rebound in the midst of a pivotal late-game run, Durant took the ball himself and made history over LeBron James with 45 seconds remaining. The clutch shot turned a two-point deficit into a one-point lead that the Warriors would not relinquish, and Durant’s 31 points, nine rebounds, four assists and four treys secured the unforgettable June 7, 2017 victory. The Warriors would go on to win the series in five games, the first of two straight titles and Finals MVP awards for Durant.

Due for a bit of comfort after surviving a grueling six-game road trip, the Philadelphia 76ers were wise to assume that, temporarily at least, all traveling would be reserved for a different day. That is, until Kevin Durant took their defense for a ride by winning a perfectly-planned footrace in transition. Seasoned in his ability to read the floor, the NBA’s eighth-highest all-time scoring leader begins his downfloor stride immediately after Paul George’s misfired 3-pointer goes collected. Completely unbothered by the trio of white jerseys encircling him during a one-on-three transition take, Durant works urgently, gathering through the paint for a ferocious one-handed flush. As the bullet points on his Hall of Fame-bound résumé have long confirmed, Durant possessed exactly what the Phoenix Suns needed to awaken from a sluggish offensive start, and subsequently, a double-digit deficit. Turned up a few rungs during Phoenix’s comeback, the four-time scoring champion mixed efficiency and effectiveness, tallying 23 points (on just 14 attempts), alongside six rebounds, five assists, one steal, one block, and three triples on January 6, 2025.

In his fifth season, Durant catches the inbound from the right wing and buries a three over the defending champions with 1.4 seconds on the clock. The shot answered Vince Carter's go-ahead triple in a rematch of the previous year's Western Conference Finals. This moment sparked the season where Durant avenged that defeat, won his third straight scoring title, earned All-Star MVP, and led the Thunder to their first Finals appearance in franchise history.

From his supporters and teammates to even himself, Kevin Durant would be forgiven if he didn’t remember the precise details associated with every score that augmented his journey to nearly 30,000 career points. Yet, even for the man with too many buckets to count, one could argue that his work on March 20, 2024 was of the unforgettable type. Chronicled through history with a highlight from every spot on the hardwood, the four-time scoring champion works through a well-timed pindown, setting the stage for his patented midrange pull-up, and ultimately, a shot at history. High in his elevation, Durant connects, fittingly elevating himself to No. 8 on the NBA’s all-time scoring leaderboard with 28,598 points. Briefly absorbing the moment through both the home crowd’s support and a congratulatory message from the player he leapfrogged —  Hall of Fame center Shaquille O’Neal —  the 14-time All-Star refocused in on helping the Phoenix Suns sustain their double-digit grip on the way to defeating the Philadelphia 76ers. The night may have been defined by Durant passing a legend, but he also passed to his teammates, guiding a selfless offensive approach with 22 points, eight rebounds, four assists, three blocks, and two triples.

Kevin Durant makes covering large distances in mere steps look easy but that’s why he’s untouchable on offense. The silky smooth forward loses Orlando Magic wing James Ennis III with a crossover at the top of the key, then heads straight for the cup for two of the 42 points he posted in a January 16, 2021 Brooklyn Nets victory.

If Kevin Durant is on your heels in transition, you better hope he’s not able to catch up in time! The Brooklyn Nets superstar sprints back in transition following an errant pass from a teammate, catches up to his opponent and fully engulfs the ball with a spectacular rejection at the basket. Durant dropped a team-high 26 points, along with six assists and three blocks in a home matchup with the Memphis Grizzlies on January 3, 2022.

On a night when he moved into the Top 20 for most points in NBA history, it’s only fitting that Kevin Durant lit up the score sheet. Showing that vintage stroke that has made him one of the most decorated players of all time, the 12-time All-Star reminds the Memphis Grizzlies that he still has plenty left in the tank. Taking advantage of a juicy one-on-one matchup, Durant takes a couple dribbles before rising up to connect on a pure elbow jumper, passing Alex English for 20th on the all-time scoring list with 25,614 points and counting. Durant erupted for 37 points on 14-for-20 shooting, along with five rebounds and four assists in the October 24, 2022 contest.

Kevin Durant, arguably the most versatile scorer in NBA history, is no stranger to major milestones. With this drive to the cup and ensuing layup, Durant moved to 10th all time in NBA career points. The 2014 NBA MVP finished the game with 30 points and 11 assists, though his Phoenix Suns ultimately dropped the contest against the reigning NBA champion Denver Nuggets on December 1, 2023.

One season removed from a Western Conference Finals in which the Dallas Mavericks’ experience and late-game execution served as the deciding factor, Kevin Durant spent much of the 2011-12 campaign showing the defending champions just how much the tables were about to turn. Having already beaten Dallas at the buzzer with a game-winning triple during the season’s opening week, the Oklahoma City Thunder superstar prepares for a postseason-style encore in Round 1. Evaluating his options from the top of the key, Durant attempts a right-sided drive, only to be stonewalled by Shawn Marion’s tight defense. Pivoting into a Plan B, the Most Valuable Player runner-up merely keeps his dribble alive, working a spin move back to the middle before elevating into a tightly-contested, fallaway jumper, getting just enough of a friendly bounce to steal a Game One victory. Durant proved brilliant all throughout crunchtime, helping Oklahoma City turn a seven-point deficit with two-and-a-half minutes to go into a confidence-building, comeback victory on April 28, 2012. Kickstarting a postseason journey that would ultimately end with an NBA Finals appearance, the future Hall of Famer turned in 25 points, six rebounds, four assists, four blocks, and one 3-point make.

Kevin Durant’s much-anticipated Phoenix Suns debut was well worth the three-week wait. The 13-time All-Star fit in seamlessly with his new teammates as he makes an impact on both ends — first blocking a Mark Williams’ shot on the low block before burying a catch-and-shoot triple off a feed from Devin Booker on the ensuing possession. Durant 23 points on 10 for 15 shooting to go with six rebounds, two assists and two blocks in Phoenix’s 105-91 road victory over the Charlotte Hornets on March 1, 2023.

Ask defenders across the NBA, and they’ll likely agree that the only thing more difficult than defending Kevin Durant is defending him in a big-time possession in one of his sweet spots just left of the top of the key. Locked and loaded with a chance to deliver a sour note on the Utah Jazz’s In-Season Tournament plans, the former Most Valuable Player sizes up Ochai Agbaji, forcing just enough of a backpedal to ease his way into a 27-foot dagger from one of his favorite locations. In describing the game as one in which neither team played defense, the four-time scoring champion, predictably, parlayed the environment into one of his season’s best games on the way to a win on November 17, 2023. The Phoenix Suns superstar exploded for 38 points — on a remarkable 15 of 22 from the field —  with nine rebounds, nine assists, and six 3-pointers along the way.

When he’s in the zone, Kevin Durant isn’t just a threat — he’s unguardable. The Brooklyn Nets superstar works his way through the Detroit Pistons defense from the perimeter through the key and to the hoop for an up-and-under reverse layup that banks in off the glass. The basket counted for two of Durant’s 51 points, marking it as an NBA season high at the time on December 12, 2021.

Undisputed in his claim as one of the greatest scorers to ever roam the planet, Kevin Durant remains all-too-familiar with the many methods of forcing opposing defenders to touch Earth along the way. Presented with a potential fastbreak opportunity with Utah Jazz rookie Taylor Hendricks aggressively anticipating his move, the Phoenix Suns superstar freezes him with a deceptive between-the-leg dribble before eliminating his defensive stance entirely with a swift crossover on the way to a one-handed flush. In helping the Suns wrap up the Jazz on February 8, 2024, the 14-time All-Star offered up both a “Welcome to the NBA” moment and a wire-to-wire victory. All-encompassing, the legendary forward provided 31 points, eight rebounds, seven assists, three steals, two blocks, and two 3-pointers.

With his team’s title aspirations officially on the ropes and the need for a vintage performance being of the utmost priority, Kevin Durant opted to accompany his trademark offensive excellence with something of equal value on the less glamorous end. Stationed just outside the paint with his eyes peeled on the Minnesota Timberwolves’ ambitious pick-and-roll attack, the former two-time NBA Finals Most Valuable Player patrols the paint with purpose, sending Mike Conley’s layup attempt off the glass, setting up a rebound and a fastbreak 3-pointer for his teammate in quick succession. The Phoenix Suns would ultimately fall short of a season-saving victory on April 28, 2024, but not without a significant two-way performance from NBA history’s fourth-highest postseason scorer. Battling valiantly throughout the elimination game, Durant recorded 33 points, nine rebounds, five assists, four blocks, and a pair of 3-pointers across a game-high 46 minutes of play.

Fortunes, for the Philadelphia 76ers, appeared to be trending upward as they went blow-for-blow with the Western Conference’s No. 2-ranked team and enjoyed the long-awaited return of a star known across the NBA by the nickname “PG13.” That is, until they ran into the Hall of Fame-bound bucket-getter who, as defenders can attest, boasts a repertoire that can be safely rated as “E for Everyone.” Leaving every blue-jerseyed defender searching for answers on November 4, 2024, Durant prepares for the most potent strike of his 15-point final quarter avalanche yet, sizing up Guerschon Yabusele before turboing down the lane’s right side. Gifted enough to stay on course, even upon recognizing Paul George’s help rotation, the four-time scoring champion merely adjusts into an outstretched banker, supplying the Phoenix Suns with a permanent lead. Durant’s excellence reached meteoric levels during Phoenix’s crunchtime comeback, which saw both a nine-point comeback in the final five minutes, and the Suns’ fifth-consecutive win. Hotter than fish grease, Durant reeled in a 35-point showing (on trademark 14-of-20 shooting), accompanied by four rebounds, six assists, one block, and two 3-pointers.

No better time to send a message than in a battle of preseason title contenders. Just as his team crosses halfcourt to set up their offense, Brooklyn Nets forward Kevin Durant blows past his defender on the perimeter, heads straight to the hoop and plants one past Los Angeles Lakers big man Andre Drummond on April 10, 2021.

Kevin Durant and the new-look Phoenix Suns kept winning as they hurtled toward a highly-anticipated postseason run. Back in town to face the Oklahoma City Thunder, Durant leveled his former team with a vintage fourth-quarter clutch performance on both ends of the court. When the Suns turned the ball over coming up the floor, it appeared Shai Gilgeous-Alexander had an uncontested dunk before Durant chased him down and blocked him from behind to preserve a seven-point fourth quarter Phoenix lead. Durant shot 13 for 21 for a team-high 35 points — 13 of which came in the fourth quarter — to go with five rebounds, five assists and two blocks as the Suns improved to 6-0 with Durant in the fold in the 128-118 win on April 2, 2023.

Kevin Durant really can do it all. The 12-time All-Star’s scoring prowess is well-documented, but his defensive effort isn’t too shabby either — just ask Myles Turner and the Indiana Pacers. Sensing an opportunity to bail out a teammate, Durant drops into the paint from the help-side and turns aside a dunk attempt in dramatic fashion. Durant was in do-it-all mode, posting 36 points, nine rebounds and seven assists to help the Brooklyn Nets get a much-needed 116-109 victory on October 31, 2022. Durant moved into 19th place on the NBA’s all-time scoring list and also scored 25-plus points in Brooklyn’s first seven games of the season, a franchise record.

It sure didn’t take long for Kevin Durant’s winning touch to be felt by the Phoenix Suns. In just the third time suiting up for his new team, the 13-time All-Star reminded the Dallas Mavericks why he’s one of the most clutch shooters in league history. After the Mavs took a late two-point lead on an alley-oop from Luka Dončić to Dwight Powell, Durant beat Tim Hardaway Jr. off the dribble before pulling up and burying a game-winning midrange jumper from the elbow with 12.1 seconds remaining. Durant’s game-high 37 points, along with seven rebounds and three assists, allowed the Suns to stay unbeaten since his arrival in a 130-126 win on March 5, 2023. Durant moved into the top-20 on the NBA’s career scoring list in 2023.

It’s Year 15 and Kevin Durant can still make jaws hit the floor with his ability to dominate a basketball game. The Orlando Magic were the 12-time All-Star’s latest victim, as Durant picks them apart in a variety of ways — on offense, he reaches into his bag of tricks for a one-handed floater off the glass, a spot-up triple, a dribble-drive into a baseline fall-away jumper and an open mid-range shot off a behind-the-back maneuver. The two-time champion and Finals MVP comes up big on the defensive end as well, turning a rebound into a long outlet dish to Joe Harris while also blocking a shot and picking Franz Wagner’s pocket at halfcourt en route to a slam. When it was over, Durant lit Orlando up for 45 points on 19-of-24 shooting while also chipping in seven rebounds, five assists, two steals and two blocks in the 109-102 win on November 28, 2022.

Even after 15 seasons, slowing down Kevin Durant remains a futile endeavor. The Phoenix Suns acquired the 13-time All-Star in hopes of capturing the franchise’s first championship, and early returns have looked promising against the LA Clippers. In Game 3 of a First Round series, Chris Paul came up with a steal on the defensive end and ran the break with Durant, who caught Paul’s pass in stride and coasted through the paint with downhill momentum before finishing with an emphatic throwdown. Durant posted 28 points, six rebounds and five assists as the Suns took a 2-1 series lead with a 129-124 road win on April 20, 2023.

Take your eyes off Kevin Durant, get torched by a generational scorer. Firing on all cylinders in a mid-season instalment of the Battle of New York, the Brooklyn Nets superstar hits a defensive gap after catching the ball on the perimeter, then racks up two of his 53 points in the form of an emphatic slam over a late help-side defender. In addition to the offensive barrage, Durant chipped in six boards and nine assists in the victory.

With respects to the other 29 teams across 2007-08’s NBA landscape, it’s unlikely that Kevin Durant could’ve asked for a more challenging introduction than the one he received against the NBA’s No. 2-ranked offense on October 31, 2007. Toe-to-toe against the soon-to-be Hall of Famer that he modeled his playstyle after, Durant responded in a similar manner to that of every great before him: by creating big-time sequences of his own. Assured of at least a 20-point performance upon rolling out of bed, the Seattle SuperSonics’ new franchise face blended pull-ups, spot-ups, and powerful attacks of the rim into his debut reel, allowing those in green-and-yellow to remain competitive until the final minutes. Though short-lived, the Rookie of the Year’s tenure in Seattle —  one that Durant has expressed interest in resuming someday — served as a memorable first footnote in his Springboard-bound career. In a season-opening loss to the Denver Nuggets, Durant acquainted himself with the box score’s every part, collecting a 18-point, five-rebound, one-assist, three-steal, one-block, two-triple showing, planting the seeds for every award imaginable over the ensuing decade.

Already as unguardable as they come, given his 6-foot-11 frame and almost-never-before-seen offensive arsenal, Kevin Durant has designed a Hall of Fame-bound career out of — in more ways than one — his ability to see over the top of opponents. On February 11, 2025, that 17-year run of bucket-getting artistry allowed access to a different type of view: a spot alongside just seven others on NBA history’s 30,000-point mountain. In need of only a measly-for-him 26-point requirement, Durant turned the nationally-broadcast battle into a New Year’s Eve-type countdown, crossing the milestone through a pair of free throws in the late third quarter to prompt a well-deserved standing ovation thereafter. As is often the case, the Phoenix Suns’ megastar incorporated doses of everything, from signature pull-ups and fearless around-the-rim attacks, to deficit-trimming triples on no-look dimes from his fellow all-world teammates. Victory wouldn’t be attained against the Memphis Grizzlies, but Durant, graciously receiving the basketball at game’s end, accomplished almost everything else, closing the evening with a 34-point masterpiece (on 12-of-18 shooting), alongside a three-rebound, three-assist, one-steal, five-block, three-trifecta complement.

Even 23-point leads in the second half aren’t safe when the man known as “The Slim Reaper” is in the building. Using a breathtaking 30-point second half to inch closer and closer to the Chicago Bulls’ advantage, the Mount Rushmore-level scorer decides to save his best for last, putting on the ultimate show of concentration with a double-clutch pull-up over two defenders. Snatching victory from the jaws of defeat, the four-time scoring champion ignited for a season-best 43 points, along with six rebounds, eight assists, one steal, two blocks, and six 3-pointers, helping the Phoenix Suns extend their winning streak to six in a vintage outing on January 22, 2024.

Welcome back, KD! In his first official game since rupturing his Achilles tendon in Game 5 of the 2019 NBA Finals, Kevin Durant of the Brooklyn Nets squares up and hits a deep three pointer for his first bucket of the night against the Golden State Warriors on December 22, 2020. Durant showed no rust from his time off, finishing with 22 points in just 25 minutes of action.

It’s a rough day at the office when you’re tasked with checking Kevin Durant. The two-time NBA Champion puts his length and footwork on display against the Denver Nuggets on January 12, 2021. The fact that the Brooklyn Nets star has one of the wettest jumpers in the league is a bonus.

The dagger! With his team trailing by two points with less than 10 seconds to play, Oklahoma City Thunder superstar Kevin Durant pulls up from deep and nails the game-winning three pointer in double overtime against the Toronto Raptors on March 21, 2014. Durant finished with a big-time 51 points on the night.

Kevin Durant is an all-time bucket getter. The Brooklyn Nets All-Star splits a pair of Washington Wizards to attack baseline then throws a hammer down on a contesting Davis Bertans on January 31, 2021.
